gen-dafont-eraser-gf-lexend-mega: Heavy, uniform-stroke letters give Eraser a blunt, understated punch. Lexend Mega, plain sans with lowercase nearly as tall as the capitals, can be sized down a notch without losing presence.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-lexend-zetta: Eraser hits hard but quietly, its bold strokes never swelling or thinning. Lexend Zetta does the opposite job, spacing out its tall-bodied small letters in wide tracking so text stays approachable while Eraser carries the weight.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-anek-kannada: Flat, stencil-cut and tightly packed: that's Bevellier. Anek Kannada, plain sans with a high lowercase and terminals that stop well short of the stem, reads with a steady, open rhythm line after line.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-nag-mundar: Sophisticated and graceful, Bevellier is flat-cut and tightly spaced. Beside it, Noto Sans Nag Mundari feels looser and more contemporary, its lowercase rivalling the capitals while the heading stays stencil-crisp.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-vai: Crisp stencil cuts, packed tight: that's Bevellier. Bevellier does display flair best, while Noto Sans Vai, with generous gaps where its curves end, makes running text settle into solid blocks.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-oxygen: Stencil-flat and tightly spaced: that's Bevellier. Bevellier is best at making a graceful statement, while Oxygen, a sans-serif with lowercase nearly matching the capitals, is best at clean, contemporary text.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-radio-canada: Stencil-cut, flat and graceful: that's Bevellier. Radio Canada keeps lowercase c, s and z tall and full with a steady line, so extended reading feels clear and unhurried.
gen-fs-expose-gf-noto-sans-old-italic: Noto Sans Old Italic keeps its curve endings well apart. Expose adds a compressed, striking cadence, and the shared tiny gap between lowercase and caps is what ties the two together.
gen-fs-expose-gf-readex-pro: Compressed and striking: Expose barely pauses between letters. Readex Pro, a sans-serif with broad gaps at its terminals, supplies the best quality here: a single-width stroke that lets Expose's tight rhythm stand out.
gen-fs-expose-gf-sen: Tight, striking and refined: Expose barely stops for breath. Sen, plain sans built tall in the lowercase with constant-weight lines, does the steady reading work that Expose's compressed display never could.
